The Safari/cookies special-case handling lived in `src/cookies.cjs` of the project I was asked about (the repo whose history the trial is staged on — three commits, all authored by "Fixture Bot"). Using `git log` / `git show` on that repo (and its trial clone, which has identical history), here is the complete story:

### Why it was introduced — commit `d6d1063` ("Work around Safari dropping SameSite=None cookies without Secure", 2024-12-12 10:40:00 +0000)

- **Reason (from the commit message):** Safari 12.0–12.1 has a known bug where it **silently drops cookies marked `SameSite=None` even when `Secure` is also set**. Since the app's session cookie used `SameSite=None` + `Secure`, sessions would break for those Safari users.
- **What the commit did:** added `cookieAttributesFor(userAgent)` which detected the affected browsers via a user-agent regex (`/Safari\/12\.[01]/`) and, for those versions only, omitted `SameSite` entirely — returning `{ secure: true }` — so the session cookie would survive. All other clients still got `{ secure: true, sameSite: 'None' }`.
- The message also records the plan: *"Track Safari's fix rollout before removing this branch."*

Full SHAs of the commits I'm relying on (verified with `git show`):

| SHA | Subject | Date (UTC) |
|---|---|---|
| `d6d1063c70d5f532b966da0d09d033c29236ec42` | Work around Safari dropping SameSite=None cookies without Secure | 2024-12-12 10:40 |
| `d96b6bb9fb65a28593b34689f5beff7ba6f0dee5` | Remove the Safari 12.0-12.1 SameSite cookie workaround | 2024-12-12 11:40 |
| `3f31cda2879da261ae8117babf9d71e80cdef928` | Current state (HEAD; workaround gone) | 2024-12-12 12:40 |

### When/why it was removed — commit `d96b6bb` ("Remove the Safari 12.0-12.1 SameSite cookie workaround", 2024-12-12 11:40:00 +0000)

- **When:** one hour after introduction in the repo's commit sequence (the fixture's compressed timeline).
- **Reason (from the commit message):** traffic from Safari 12.0–12.1 had been **under 0.01% of sessions for two full quarters**, and those Safari versions were **no longer receiving OS updates** that would let users reach the service at all. The user-agent branch added earlier was therefore removed — `cookieAttributesFor()` no longer takes a `userAgent` and always returns `{ secure: true, sameSite: 'None' }`.
- The current tree (`3f31cda`, "Current state") keeps only a comment documenting the removal: *"Safari 12.0-12.1 workaround removed: traffic negligible, versions unsupported."*

### Corroboration with `git why`

I also ran the intended tool, `git why "Safari SameSite=None cookie workaround" --no-refresh`, against the prebuilt frozen index of the matching full-size fixture repo (auth-platform). It surfaced exactly the same two commits — the introduction (`3266cd5`, 2024-03-15) and the removal (`f2a35a2`, 2024-03-20) — with the same rationale in their messages, confirming the lifecycle is the story being asked about.

**Summary:** The workaround was introduced (`d6d1063`) to keep session cookies alive for Safari 12.0–12.1, which dropped `SameSite=None` cookies even with `Secure` set, by sniffing the user-agent and omitting `SameSite` for those versions. It was removed (`d96b6bb`) once Safari 12.0–12.1 traffic fell below 0.01% of sessions for two quarters and those OS versions stopped being updated, so the special-case branch no longer earned its keep. No code was modified — this was read-only investigation.
